response.query: Which exact clinical-proxy items (fever, recent antibiotics, ICD codes, steroid use) and timeframes can reliably substitute for CRP when assays are unavailable?
response.answer: Fever, recent antibiotics, ICD code R50.8, and steroid use can substitute for CRP when assays are unavailable. Use ICD-10 code R79.82 for elevated CRP.

results.title: Elevated CRP ICD-10-CM Codes | 2025 - Carepatron
results.content: # Elevated CRP ICD-10-CM Codes Read this short guide to learn about elevated CRP ICD codes you can use. Elevated CRP ICD-10-CM Codes ## **What ICD-10 codes are used for elevated CRP?** If you're looking for elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) ICD codes, there is only one ICD-10 code specific to it, and that'sÂ **R79.82: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP).** The code is under the following categories, code ranges, chapters, etc.: Just as its name states, this ICD-10 code is meant to be used on a patient confirmed to have C-reactive protein levels that are way above the normal range. The normal range for C-reactive protein is less than 0.9 milligrams per deciliter (mg/dL). If your patient has a C-reactive protein level higher than 0.9mg/dL, you may use this ICD-10 code. Please note that this ICD-10 code is not valid as a principal diagnosis because elevated C-reactive protein commonly results from inflammation, so your primary ICD-10 code must be related to inflammation as per the guidelines to ensure proper coding practices. You may also use this for cases related to infections, tissue injuries/damage, chronic diseases, and autoimmune diseases related to CRP elevation. ## **Which elevated CRP ICD codes are billable?** Even if this ICD-10 code for Elevated CRP isn't valid as a principal diagnosis, the lone code is valid in general and billable. ## **Clinical information** C-reactive Protein, or CRP for short, is a substance produced by the liver and released into the bloodstream whenever a person has inflammation, infections, tissue injuries, chronic diseases, or autoimmune diseases. Healthcare professionals consider elevated levels of CRP as a marker for underlying problems a patient might have. Please note that only looking at CRP levels isn't enough to determine the underlying problem. Some health factors (both physical and mental) can raise CRP levels, such as depression, periodontitis, having a cold, diabetes, gingivitis, and insomnia. If the CRP level is between 1.0 and 10mg/dL, the patient might have rheumatoid arthritis, bronchitis, pancreatitis, or myocardial infarction. If the CRP level is higher than 10mg/dL, they might have physical trauma, systemic vasculitis, viral infection, or acute bacterial infection.

results.content: Home / Articles / ICD 10 / How To Use The ICD 10 Codes For Personal History Of Medical Treatment. # How To Use The ICD 10 Codes For Personal History Of Medical Treatment. *The ICD 10 CM codes under the category Z92 pertain to personal histories of various medical treatments, which are essential for documenting a patient’s previous medical interventions. The ICD 10 CM category Z92 encompasses personal histories of medical treatments that have implications for ongoing patient management. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.2:** Personal history of drug therapy. *Clinical Context:* General code for any drug therapy history. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.22:** Personal history of monoclonal drug therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.23:** Personal history of estrogen therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.24:** Personal history of steroid therapy. *Pitfall:* Failing to specify the type of steroid therapy can lead to coding errors. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.240:** Personal history of inhaled steroid therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.241:** Personal history of systemic steroid therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.25:** Personal history of immunosuppression therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.29:** Personal history of other drug therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.8:** Personal history of other medical treatment. *Clinical Context:* General code for other medical treatments not specified elsewhere. *Pitfall:* Failing to document the timing of treatment can lead to coding errors. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.85:** Personal history of cellular therapy. *Pitfall:* Failing to document the type of cellular therapy can lead to coding errors. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.858:** Personal history of other cellular therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.859:** Personal history of cellular therapy, unspecified. *Clinical Context:* General code for unspecified cellular therapies. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.86:** Personal history of gene therapy. * **ICD 10 CM Z92.89:** Personal history of other medical treatment. *Clinical Context:* General code for other medical treatments not specified elsewhere. * Use Z92 codes specifically for documenting personal histories of medical treatments. * Differentiate between Z92 codes for drug therapies and other treatment codes (e.g., Z51 for encounters for other aftercare). **Primary Injury Code:** Z92.21 (Personal history of antineoplastic chemotherapy). **Primary Injury Code:** Z92.850 (Personal history of
